correctness.rationale: For every induced bipartite subgraph, each bounded geodesic alternates sides. The condition \(d\le2k-3\) limits either side to at most \(k-1\) vertices on such a geodesic, giving a two-color upper bound. If a geodesic hyperedge exists, it supplies a \(k\)-clique while pigeonhole plus alternation rules out \(2k-1\)-cliques, forcing the normalized clique lower bound to equal two; if no hyperedge exists, both normalized clique bound and chromatic number equal one. Boundary cases, disconnected graphs, and hereditary induced subgraphs are covered. A direct finite reconstruction of the definitions independently stress-tests the argument.

value.rationale: This gives an infinite hereditary class theorem for a newly introduced perfection notion, not a finite or parameter-by-parameter computation. It answers a substantial class of the explicit \(3,2\)-perfection problem, strictly contains the previously proved tree case, adds all bipartite graphs at \(3,3\), and identifies a simple structural mechanism valid on an infinite two-parameter strip.
